# Points Mock Draft [YAHOO] | 2026/27 NBA Fantasy Basketball

Locked On Fantasy Basketball, 2026-08-24, 46:45. https://youtu.be/g31YlwRe0XQ

## Summary

Josh Lloyd runs a 12-team Yahoo points league mock draft (Yahoo default scoring) from pick 6, and keeps pointing out how player values change between points and category leagues. He says there is a big drop after the top four in points leagues (Jokic, Doncic, Wembanyama, Giannis), and that Shai Gilgeous-Alexander sits below that group. His team is Cade Cunningham, Domantas Sabonis, Bam Adebayo, Jalen Williams, Jaren Jackson Jr., Brandon Ingram, Coby White, Norman Powell, Onyeka Okongwu, Brandon Podziemski, Jeremiah Fears, Yaxel Lendeborg, Gui Santos and Tobias Harris. He calls out reaches he disliked: Tyrese Maxey, Tyrese Haliburton, Chet Holmgren, Zion Williamson, Franz Wagner, Fred VanVleet, Dylan Harper (said as "Dron Sharp") and Kevin Porter Jr. He calls LeBron James at 52 and Brandon Ingram falling to round 6 big values. In late rounds he takes upside swings over boring veterans, and his projections rated his team the best in the room. Note that this is a points-league mock, not the 9-category format.

## Rules and methods

- [4:26](https://youtu.be/g31YlwRe0XQ?t=266) Points league and category league values differ a lot. Know your format, because drafting from category rankings in a points league can hurt you badly.
  > "this is not a category league and we'll see how players and managers approach this draft"
- [25:17](https://youtu.be/g31YlwRe0XQ?t=1517) Scoring is the number one contributor to fantasy points in points leagues, so high-usage scorers gain value there.
  > "the number one contributor to fantasy points is scoring and he's going to have a lot of usage"
- [22:56](https://youtu.be/g31YlwRe0XQ?t=1376) A reach costs more early than late. Twenty spots too high in round 3 is bad. Fifteen spots too high in round 6 hardly matters.
  > "if it's 20 spots too high in round three, bad, right? If it's 15 spots too high"
- [9:55](https://youtu.be/g31YlwRe0XQ?t=595) On the turn, reaching for a player you really want can be justified, because he will not come back to you.
  > "on the turn, you can always make arguments cuz if Harden's the guy you want, you're not going to get him"
- [38:05](https://youtu.be/g31YlwRe0XQ?t=2285) In late rounds (13 and 14), take upside swings over boring veterans. Boring players can be found later, and they become value picks outside the top 150.
  > "Let's hit some of these upside guys that might be the 90th best player, but might be 180th"
- [38:39](https://youtu.be/g31YlwRe0XQ?t=2319) Boring veterans are fine late but bad picks in early or middle rounds. Take them when they fall past their value.
  > "But if you take him at in round 10, it's just nothing. It's boring. It's not interesting."
- [39:48](https://youtu.be/g31YlwRe0XQ?t=2388) Hedge strategy: draft two players fighting for the same minutes, then drop whichever one loses the role.
  > "Do I take Yaxle and then take Santos and whoever gets the bulk of those minutes is good"
- [45:00](https://youtu.be/g31YlwRe0XQ?t=2700) A fantasy basketball handcuff, unlike one in fantasy football, must have value on his own, with big upside if the starter gets hurt.
  > "a fantasy basketball handcuff has to have value on his own with huge upside"
- [21:51](https://youtu.be/g31YlwRe0XQ?t=1311) Players with health uncertainty can be strong per game, but it is better to wait a few rounds on them.
  > "Pzingis probably per game is better than this, but I'd like to wait a few more rounds given this the health uncertainty"
